horvath_2013.cite: Horvath S (2013). DNA methylation age of human tissues and cell types. Genome Biology 14(10):R115.
horvath_2013.verified_via: NCBI esearch (DOI->PMID) + efetch full-text XML (PMC4015143), live this session
horvath_2013.numbers: 353 CpGs; 8,000 samples, 82 Illumina DNAm array datasets, 51 healthy tissues/cell types (training). Training-data accuracy: age correlation r=0.97, median absolute error=2.9y. Held-out TEST-data (unbiased): r=0.96, error=3.6y. Per-tissue breakdown: PBMC r=0.97(err<1y), whole blood r=0.98(err=2.7y), cerebellum r=0.92(err=4.5y), pons r=0.96(err=3.3y), prefrontal cortex r=0.98(err=1.4y), temporal cortex r=0.99(err=2.2y), mixed brain r=0.94(err=3.1y), stomach r=0.84(err=3.7y), thyroid r=0.96(err=4.1y). DNAm age ~0 for ESC/iPSC; correlates with cell passage number; applicable to chimpanzee tissue.

horvath_2013_erratum.cite: Horvath S (2015). Erratum to: DNA methylation age of human tissues and cell types. Genome Biology 16:96.
horvath_2013_erratum.verified_via: NCBI esearch (DOI->PMID) + efetch full-text XML (PMC4427927), live this session
horvath_2013_erratum.numbers: Software coding error affected ONLY the cancer-tissue age-acceleration DIRECTION analysis (added a systematic offset via wrong calibration function for cancer datasets); author explicitly retracts the claim that most cancer types show increased DNAm age acceleration (direction is mixed, not uniformly positive). Author states verbatim: results involving non-cancerous tissue or cancer cell lines remain valid -- i.e. this doc's core accuracy numbers (r=0.96/0.97, MAE=2.9/3.6y, 51-tissue breakdown) are explicitly outside the correction's scope. The original abstract's '20 cancer types, average 36 years acceleration' figure is retracted and is NOT repeated in this doc's claims.

hannum_2013.cite: Hannum G et al (2013). Genome-wide methylation profiles reveal quantitative views of human aging rates. Molecular Cell 49(2):359-367.
hannum_2013.verified_via: NCBI esearch (DOI->PMID) + efetch abstract, live this session
hannum_2013.numbers: Whole blood, 656 individuals, ages 19-101; >450,000 CpG markers screened; final model uses 71 CpGs (cross-confirmed via Chen2016 Methods, since Hannum's own abstract does not state the final CpG count). Blood-only training design; abstract claims secondary generalization ('upheld in other human tissues') without a specific accuracy figure for that claim.

marioni_2015.cite: Marioni RE et al (2015). DNA methylation age of blood predicts all-cause mortality in later life. Genome Biology 16:25.
marioni_2015.verified_via: NCBI esearch + efetch full-text XML (PMC4350614), live this session
marioni_2015.numbers: 4 cohorts: LBC1921 N=446/292 deaths, LBC1936 N=920/106 deaths, FHS N=2635/238 deaths, NAS N=657/226 deaths (total N~4658). Age+sex-adjusted HR per 5y {Delta}age: Hannum 1.21 (95%CI 1.14-1.29,P<0.0001), Horvath 1.11 (95%CI 1.05-1.18,P=0.0003). Fully adjusted (childhood IQ, education, social class, hypertension, diabetes, CVD, APOE e4): Hannum 1.16 (95%CI 1.08-1.25,P=6.0e-9), Horvath 1.09 (95%CI 1.02-1.15,P=0.0069). Heritability: Horvath h2=0.43(SE.07,P=9e-13), Hannum h2=0.42(SE.07,P=4e-10) (BSGS cohort). Void-floor comparator in the SAME 4 cohorts: Weidner predictor R=0.02-0.43, MAE=12.6-29.9y, 'not examined further' by the paper's own authors.

chen_2016.cite: Chen BH et al (2016). DNA methylation-based measures of biological age: meta-analysis predicting time to death. Aging (Albany NY) 8(9):1844-1865.
chen_2016.verified_via: NCBI esearch + efetch full-text XML (PMC5076441), live this session
chen_2016.numbers: 13 cohorts, N=13,089, 2734 deaths (21%), 3 racial/ethnic groups (non-Hispanic white n=9215 + Hispanic + African American). All epigenetic age-acceleration measures predictive of mortality independent of chronological age: univariate P<=8.2e-9, fully-adjusted P<5.4e-4. EEAA (cell-composition-corrected, Hannum-based) strongest: HR=1.040 per 1y EEAA (i.e. HR=1.48 for EEAA=10, HR=0.82 for EEAA=-5); smallest reported p-value 7.5e-43. Horvath-Hannum inter-correlation r=0.76 despite sharing only 6/(353+71) CpGs. Per-cohort age-correlation ~0.6-0.8 (e.g. WHI-White Horvath r=0.67, Hannum r=0.73) -- lower than Horvath's original 0.96, an honest disclosed real-world attenuation in older/blood-only/narrower-range cohorts. Paper's own caveat: HRs across differently-scaled measures are not directly comparable.

levine_2018_phenoage.cite: Levine ME et al (2018). An epigenetic biomarker of aging for lifespan and healthspan. Aging (Albany NY) 10(4):573-591.
levine_2018_phenoage.verified_via: NCBI esearch + efetch abstract, live this session
levine_2018_phenoage.numbers: 2nd-gen clock trained on a 9-biomarker mortality/phenotype composite (not raw age). Abstract claims: 'strongly outperforms previous measures' for all-cause mortality, cancers, healthspan, physical functioning, Alzheimer's disease; 'correlates strongly with age in every tissue and cell tested' (independent corroboration of cross-tissue tracking from a different CpG panel than Horvath's).

lu_2019_grimage.cite: Lu AT et al (2019). DNA methylation GrimAge strongly predicts lifespan and healthspan. Aging (Albany NY) 11(2):303-327.
lu_2019_grimage.verified_via: NCBI esearch + efetch full-text XML (PMC6366976), live this session
lu_2019_grimage.numbers: 2nd-gen clock: 7 DNAm-surrogate plasma proteins + DNAm-estimated smoking pack-years, Cox time-to-death trained. Construction/test cohort: FHS Offspring N=2356 (training 1731/622 pedigrees, test 625/266 pedigrees). Time-to-death Cox P=2.0e-75 ('thousands of individuals' in validation per abstract, exact combined n not stated -- honest gap); time-to-CHD P=6.2e-24; time-to-cancer P=1.3e-12; age-at-menopause P=1.6e-12; comorbidity count P=3.45e-17. GrimAge correlates with chronological age at r=0.82 (lower than Horvath's 0.96/0.97) and with DNAm TIMP-1 r=0.90. AgeAccelGrim vs Horvath-clock-acceleration cross-correlation r=0.17 (weak) -- quantifies the cross-generation partial independence.

mccrory_2021_tilda.cite: McCrory C et al (2021). GrimAge Outperforms Other Epigenetic Clocks in the Prediction of Age-Related Clinical Phenotypes and All-Cause Mortality. J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci 76(5):741-749.
mccrory_2021_tilda.verified_via: NCBI esearch (author+title/abstract terms) + efetch abstract, live this session
mccrory_2021_tilda.numbers: TILDA cohort n=490, up to 10y follow-up, 9 clinical/mortality outcomes, 4 clocks (Horvath/Hannum/PhenoAge/GrimAge) tested head-to-head, same methods, cohort independent of any clock's own training data. Result: HorvathAA and HannumAA not predictive of health/mortality (0/9); PhenoAgeAA 4/9 minimally-adjusted, loses significance fully adjusted; GrimAgeAA 8/9 minimally-adjusted (all except grip strength), retains significance fully adjusted for walking speed, polypharmacy, frailty, AND mortality specifically.

higgins_chen_2022_pcclock.cite: Higgins-Chen AT et al (2022). A computational solution for bolstering reliability of epigenetic clocks. Nature Aging 2(7):644-661.
higgins_chen_2022_pcclock.verified_via: NCBI esearch + efetch abstract, live this session
higgins_chen_2022_pcclock.numbers: Technical noise produces deviations up to 9 years between replicate measurements of the SAME sample, across 6 prominent epigenetic clocks. Retrained principal-component (PC) versions of the same 6 clocks show agreement between most replicates within 1.5 years. Platform/normalization-dependence anchor; this repo's graph already encodes it as a formal gate (AUTO-CLOCK-CONSTRUCT-VALIDITY-GATE-FOR-ANY-EP, cross-referenced not edited).

jaffe_irizarry_2014_heterogeneity.cite: Jaffe AE, Irizarry RA (2014). Accounting for cellular heterogeneity is critical in epigenome-wide association studies. Genome Biology 15(2):R31.
jaffe_irizarry_2014_heterogeneity.verified_via: NCBI esearch + efetch abstract, live this session
jaffe_irizarry_2014_heterogeneity.numbers: Blood is a heterogeneous mix of cell types with very different methylation profiles; cell composition changes with age in blood; cell composition explains much of DNAm variability; high confounding between age-related methylation changes and cell composition at the CpG level. Anchors the tissue-heterogeneity-confounds-blood-clocks symmetric-QC item; motivates why cell-composition-corrected measures (IEAA/EEAA) exist and why Chen2016 found EEAA strongest.

symmetric_qc_open_items: Causality (clock as cause vs marker of aging): genuinely unresolved, held OPEN by design, not adjudicated by this doc.

Array-platform + normalization dependence: up to 9y technical noise between replicates (Higgins-Chen 2022), ~1.5y after PC-correction -- a real floor against which small intervention effects must be judged.

Tissue heterogeneity (blood-cell-composition drift with age) confounds naive whole-blood clocks (Jaffe & Irizarry 2014) -- motivates and is partially addressed by composition-corrected variants (IEAA/EEAA).
2nd-gen clocks' mortality-prediction edge is partly a by-construction effect of their training target, not purely a discovered latent 'pace of aging' -- disclosed, not hidden, in Falsifier 3.
